samples.claim: size returns (len + spare capacity in the last Vec)*size_of::<T>() + size_of::<Self>() + number_of_blocks*size_of::<Vec<T>>(). The comments describe allocated element capacity and warn that nested heap contents such as String data are absent. The formula counts the complete inline T representation, not a String allocation. It omits LinkedList link-node overhead and allocator overhead; it is an estimate, not exact total retained memory. The formula assumes earlier blocks contribute their live length, not all earlier spare capacity.
samples.evidence:
109 | 
110 |     /// Returns the size of list, including the size of the elements and the
111 |     /// size of the list itself, and the unused space.
112 |     /// The element size is calculated using `std::mem::size_of::<T>()`,
113 |     /// so it is not accurate for all types.
114 |     /// For example, for `String`, it will return the size of the pointer,
115 |     /// not the size of the string itself. For that you need to use `DeepSizeOf`.
116 |     pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
117 |         let unused_space = match self.inner.back() {
118 |             Some(last) => last.capacity() - last.len(),
119 |             None => 0,
120 |         };
121 |         (self.len() + unused_space) * std::mem::size_of::<T>()
122 |             + std::mem::size_of::<Self>()
123 |             + self.inner.len() * std::mem::size_of::<Vec<T>>()
124 |     }
samples.review_note: Matches exact arithmetic; last-block spare capacity only, no linked-list node or nested heap allocation accounting.

samples.claim: Public CountsMatrix derives Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq with private destination count, block rows, total old physical rows u64 (including deleted), and row-major cumulative Vec<u32>. Each matrix row is through the end of a block, unlike the exclusive count-before accessor. Deleted counts are implicit differences from physical row budgets.
samples.evidence:
87 | 
88 | /// Cumulative per-destination row counts at every block boundary.
89 | ///
90 | /// Row `b` of the grid holds, for each destination label `d`, the number of
91 | /// source rows labeled `d` in blocks `0..=b`. The final row therefore holds
92 | /// the total row count of every destination. Deleted (NULL-labeled) rows are
93 | /// not counted; the deleted count of a block is implied by
94 | /// `block length - sum of per-label deltas`.
95 | #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
96 | pub struct CountsMatrix {
97 |     /// Number of destinations `m`; labels are `0..m`.
98 |     num_destinations: u32,
99 |     /// Source rows per block. Only the final block may be shorter.
100 |     block_rows: u32,
101 |     /// Total physical source rows, including deleted rows.
102 |     total_rows: u64,
103 |     /// `num_blocks * num_destinations` cumulative counts, row-major by block.
104 |     cumulative: Vec<u32>,
105 | }
106 |
samples.review_note: Matches private field types, inclusive cumulative rows and implicit deletion counts. Supplementary129-148 confirms exclusive count_before.

samples.claim: Default remap_row_ids(&self,&[u64])->Result<Vec<Option<u64>>> reserves input length, iterates in input order and sequentially awaits remap_row_id, pushing one result per input. Duplicates and None positions are preserved, empty input gives empty Vec, and the first Err stops iteration and discards the partial result. There is no concurrent buffering or aggregation. Cancellation can interrupt an in-flight single-row future; the trait makes no rollback promise for implementation side effects.
samples.review_note: Matches sequential awaits, positional preservation and early Result propagation; no rollback machinery.

samples.claim: MIN_SHARD_SHARE=4<<30 usize (4GiB) expresses desired shard budget; source warns heavy entries may be silently unadmitted because shards cannot borrow capacity. Public recommended_cache_shards queries available_parallelism, falls back2 on error, then delegates pure sizing. No environment variable override is read here. The constant itself assumes usize can represent4GiB; this file does not demonstrate32-bit target support.
samples.evidence:
61 | /// Minimum weight budget (4 GiB) per shard: shards don't borrow capacity, and
62 | /// an entry heavier than ~its shard's budget is silently refused admission.
63 | const MIN_SHARD_SHARE: usize = 4 << 30;
64 | 
65 | /// Recommended shard count: `min(cpus / 2, capacity / 4 GiB)`, power of two
66 | /// in `[1, 1024]`. The cpu term bounds lock contention; the capacity term
67 | /// keeps each shard's budget >= 4 GiB so large entries stay admissible.
68 | /// Rounded down because quick_cache rounds requests up.
69 | pub fn recommended_cache_shards(capacity: usize) -> usize {
70 |     let available_parallelism = std::thread::available_parallelism()
71 |         .map(|n| n.get())
72 |         .unwrap_or(2);
73 |     recommended_cache_shards_for_parallelism(capacity, available_parallelism)
74 | }
75 |
samples.review_note: Matches usize4GiB constant, available_parallelism fallback2 and delegation; no 32-bit build claim.

samples.claim: MemWalIndexDetails centralizes configuration, base compaction progress, and shard snapshots. Background refresh does not make snapshots authoritative mutable shard state. Snapshot Lance-file schema lists shard_id utf8, shard_spec_id uint32, typed shard_field_{id}. snapshot_ts_millis int64=1 and num_shards uint32=2 describe it; optional inline_snapshots bytes=3 holds Lance bytes for small counts. The threshold example 100 is explicitly implementation-defined, not a specified constant.

samples.claim: build_predicate receives slice::Iter<u64>. Bitmap/Set compute !contains(id as u32) for every address into Vec<bool>, then convert to BooleanArray: true means retain/not deleted, false deleted, and values are non-null. Casting discards the high fragment half, so callers must apply the single-fragment deletion vector to the correct fragment. NoDeletions returns None, but an empty Set/Bitmap returns Some(all true), including Some(empty) on empty input. This is not a fragment-ID validator or a stable-row-ID remapper.
samples.evidence:
104 | 
105 |     // Note: deletion vectors are based on 32-bit offsets.  However, this function works
106 |     // even when given 64-bit row addresses.  That is because `id as u32` returns the lower
107 |     // 32 bits (the row offset) and the upper 32 bits are ignored.
108 |     pub fn build_predicate(&self, row_addrs: std::slice::Iter<u64>) -> Option<BooleanArray> {
109 |         match self {
110 |             Self::Bitmap(bitmap) => Some(
111 |                 row_addrs
112 |                     .map(|&id| !bitmap.contains(id as u32))
113 |                     .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
114 |             ),
115 |             Self::Set(set) => Some(
116 |                 row_addrs
117 |                     .map(|&id| !set.contains(&(id as u32)))
118 |                     .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
119 |             ),
120 |             Self::NoDeletions => None,
121 |         }
122 |         .map(BooleanArray::from)
123 |     }
124 | }
samples.review_note: Matches low32 conversion, retain polarity, Vec<bool> construction and distinct None/empty-container results.
